title: Bhishma's fall
hook: Krishna promised not to fight. Then he jumps down from the chariot and runs at Bhishma, and Bhishma welcomes him.

segments.voice: Yesterday Bhishma's fall began as a riddle: a commander who loves the other side, Karna waiting in his tent, and a man who dies only when he chooses. Which promise did you keep? Day eight hundred twenty-six.
screen: `A RIDDLE, NOT YET A FALL.` · `DEATH WHEN HE CHOOSES.`

segments.voice: A charioteer's work is the reins. Krishna came to this war with one promise: he would not take up a weapon. He drives the chariot, he talks, and in the Gita he taught. But he doesn't fight. Then, early in the battle, Bhishma is cutting through the Pandava ranks, and Arjuna is holding back. And Krishna leaps down from the chariot and runs at Bhishma on foot. Today: the day the driver breaks his word, and the man he runs at welcomes him.
screen: `KRISHNA CAME UNARMED` → `ARJUNA HOLDS BACK` → `THE DRIVER JUMPS DOWN`

segments.voice: Here's how it happens in Ganguli's telling. Duryodhana has accused Bhishma of going easy on the Pandavas, and the old man is stung. So he fights like fire. And Arjuna, facing the grandfather he grew up with, fights gently. He can't make himself strike hard. Krishna sees the Pandava army breaking. He drops the reins, jumps down, and rushes at Bhishma with his discus raised. Now watch Bhishma. He doesn't flinch. He stands his ground, bow in hand, and calls out a welcome. Come, he says to Krishna. Strike me down. To be killed by you would be an honor. Think about that. The enemy commander greets the attack with something close to joy. Then Arjuna jumps down after Krishna, grabs him, and holds on. He's dragged along the ground until Krishna finally stops. Arjuna begs him to turn back, and swears he'll fight in earnest. Krishna climbs back into the chariot. And it doesn't end there. Days later, it happens again. Bhishma is unstoppable, Arjuna is still too gentle, and Krishna leaps down once more, this time with nothing in his hand but his horse whip. Bhishma welcomes him again. Arjuna pulls him back again. Some later retellings add that Bhishma had sworn to make Krishna break his vow. Whatever you make of that, the scene in the text is plain enough. The teacher who told Arjuna to do his duty without wavering is pushed so far by his student's holding back that he nearly breaks his own word. And the man everyone is trying to stop is the one on the field who seems least afraid.
screen: `ARJUNA FIGHTS TOO GENTLY` · `KRISHNA RUNS AT BHISHMA` · `BHISHMA: COME, STRIKE ME DOWN` · then, large: `ARJUNA HOLDS HIM BACK, TWICE`

segments.voice: Sit and let your breath settle. This is the end of a week that began with the Gita's first chapter, a man sitting down in his chariot, and ends with a teacher jumping out of one. Look back over your own week. Find one moment when you held back, and one when you moved. Breathing in, see the first. Breathing out, see the second. You don't have to judge either. Just let them sit side by side. If you pray, you can offer both in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma's fall. Still not yet. Today it's a man so ready for death that he welcomes the one who comes to bring it.
Your line: Bhishma's fall. Today, notice one place where you've been holding back, and take one real step instead. Day eight hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: The scene of Krishna leaping from the chariot toward Bhishma, and Bhishma welcoming him, is told in the Bhishma book of the Mahabharata and appears in paintings and retellings of the war.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. your driver, who promised not to fight, has jumped down and is running at your grandfather. what do you do?
options: let him go: Bhishma has to be stopped.
jump down, grab him, and promise to fight in earnest.
fork.reveal: Arjuna jumps down and holds on until Krishna stops, then swears to fight properly. Krishna climbs back into the chariot.

original.note: Sudarshana, Krishna's discus, which he raises the first time he runs at Bhishma.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna never broke his promise not to fight.
what it means: he nearly did, twice, and Arjuna held him back each time.
what a scholar hears: some readers see the scene as Krishna putting his devotee's need above his own vow.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: the first charge (third day) follows Duryodhana's reproach and Arjuna's mild fighting; Krishna takes up the discus (Sudarshana) and rushes at Bhishma; Bhishma welcomes him ('come, O lotus-eyed one... slain by thee I shall be honored'); Arjuna seizes him and Krishna stops; Arjuna vows to fight. The second charge (ninth day): Krishna leaps down with only the whip; Bhishma welcomes him again; Arjuna restrains him.
The script avoids day numbers ('early in the battle', 'days later'). It says Arjuna is 'dragged along the ground'; confirm the detail (Ganguli has Arjuna seizing Krishna's legs and being dragged).
The line about Bhishma's vow to make Krishna take up arms is labeled as from 'later retellings'; confirm the Keeper is comfortable naming it, or cut.
Week-end look-back is in the practice (week of days 820–826).

Editor pass: Ganguli has Bhishma drawing his bow as he welcomes Krishna, so 'doesn't defend himself' and 'opens his arms' became 'stands his ground, bow in hand' and 'calls out a welcome', and the myth item was rewritten; cut the hook's and a myth item's callback to Arjuna choosing Krishna in the Udyoga days, which repeated day 821's hook.

Audit (fresh pass): the teach ended by repeating 'calls out a welcome'; ending rewritten. 'So moved by his student's wavering' read as tenderness the text doesn't give (Krishna acts as the army breaks); now 'pushed so far'. Sudarshana pronunciation completed.
